skill.name: turn-this-into-a-thread
skill.description: Turn a long idea, transcript, article or rambling draft into a Twitter thread where every tweet earns the next one. Use when someone asks for a thread, asks to break something long into tweets, or has a piece of writing too long for one post. Do not use it for LinkedIn, which has no threads, and do not pad a small idea into a long thread.
skill.summary: Turn long-form ideas into concise, connected Twitter threads.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Turn Long Ideas Into Strong Threads
content.value_statement: Long drafts often lose readers when they are divided into arbitrary tweets. This skill finds the core sequence and shapes each tweet into a connected, standalone post.
actual_capabilities: Decide whether an idea deserves a thread or a single post.
Extract a clear sequence of beats from long source material.
Write standalone tweets with a specific opening and connected progression.
Format tweets with three-dash separators for manual posting or VoiceMOAT.
Adapt connected VoiceMOAT workflows for voice scoring, improvement, publishing, and scheduling.
limitations: It is designed for Twitter threads, not LinkedIn posts or other formats.
It cannot verify factual claims, sources, or legal and editorial risks.
It needs enough source material to identify a meaningful sequence.
Voice scoring, publishing, and scheduling require a connected VoiceMOAT Pro or Enterprise plan.

use_cases.title: Repurpose an Article
use_cases.description: Convert a detailed article into a focused thread with a strong hook, clear progression, and useful closing.

use_cases.title: Shape a Personal Story
use_cases.description: Turn a rough story or transcript into a sequence where each tweet stands alone and advances the narrative.

use_cases.title: Teach a Multi-Step Idea
use_cases.description: Structure a complex lesson into distinct beats without padding the thread or losing the central argument.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Thread Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this idea into a concise Twitter thread. First decide whether it needs a thread. Use only the strongest points and separate tweets with three dashes.

prompt_templates.title: Article to Thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the source below into a Twitter thread. Identify the central claim, outline five to nine beats, then write standalone tweets with a clear opening and closing.

prompt_templates.title: Story Thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Shape this transcript into a narrative Twitter thread. Preserve the meaningful turns, remove repetition, avoid generic thread openings, and ensure each tweet works when read alone.

prompt_templates.title: VoiceMoat Publishing Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this draft into a Twitter thread for VoiceMOAT. Keep the three-dash separators, use my Twitter voice profile, score the result, improve weak tweets, and prepare it for preview before publishing.

output_examples.input: A rough explanation of why small teams should document decisions.
output: Small teams do not need more meetings. They need fewer repeated decisions.
A short decision record preserves the context that disappears from memory.
That record lets the team move quickly without reopening the same debate.

output_examples.input: A founder transcript about abandoning a popular feature.
output_examples.output: A narrative thread that opens with the feature decision, explains the evidence, shows the reversal, and closes with the lesson for other builders.

output_examples.input: A long tutorial about evaluating a new software tool.
output: Start with the evaluation question, not the tool name.
Define the user problem before comparing features.
End with a practical decision rule readers can apply.

best_practices: Provide the full source and identify the intended audience.
State whether the thread should sound personal, instructional, or analytical.
Review every tweet for accuracy, standalone clarity, and unnecessary repetition.
anti_patterns: Do not split an article into tweets without creating a meaningful sequence.
Do not stretch one small point into an artificial long thread.
Do not use a LinkedIn-style register or generic opening language for Twitter.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a source contains a genuine sequence, story, or group of distinct points that works well across multiple tweets.

faq.question: Can it tell me when a thread is unnecessary?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend a single post when the idea has only one point and one supporting detail.

faq.question: What separator does it use?
faq.answer: It separates tweets with a line containing three dashes, which VoiceMOAT can use to chain the thread.

faq.question: Does it write for LinkedIn?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for Twitter threads and should not be used to create LinkedIn content.

faq.question: Can it match my writing voice?
faq.answer: Voice matching is available through the connected VoiceMOAT Twitter profile and requires a Pro or Enterprise plan.

faq.question: Can it publish the finished thread?
faq.answer: A connected VoiceMOAT account can preview, confirm, publish, or schedule the thread.
